objects.summary: P1 cost-diagnostic review finds single-use artifact omits preregistered diagnostics such as drawdown, monetary/per-turnover costs, total break-even and per-session notional/side/ADV/participation/shortfall; without persisting them the non-rerunnable result cannot be fully audited.

P2 cost-model review finds central scenario does not exactly reuse ExecutionModel.fill: commission is recomputed on reference notional instead of fill-adjusted price and sell quantity sign is lost, so claimed FILLS equivalence can differ near thresholds.

P2 review finds B4 L=21/63/126 comparison lookbacks receive indistinguishable COST_* statuses despite E4 fixing L=252 as selected; result must persist role=selected versus comparison_only_not_for_selection to prevent post-hoc reselection.

P1 scientific review rejects blanket FAMILY_REJECTED when the test lacks preregistered power to detect a plausible effect; failure to reach t threshold under severe power limits should be INCONCLUSIVE_UNDERPOWERED for the tested specification rather than proof the entire causal family is absent.

P1 multiplicity review finds dataset-level trial count charges all prior B2 expressions to a causally distinct B4 family while a dataset change resets debt. It recommends alpha budgets/counters identified by cohort and family plus a separately controlled global budget.

cross_object_findings.finding: When rerun is forbidden, an artifact that omits preregistered diagnostics cannot be reconstructed later without violating the single-use design; auditability must be designed before execution.
Calling an existing execution model but recomputing some cost posts differently is not semantic reuse. Exact desk accounting and signed order semantics must remain bound to the claimed model.
Publishing alternative specifications without role labels creates a post-hoc reselection channel even when the preregistration froze one selected candidate.
Scientific rigor must distinguish failure to confirm from evidence of absence; otherwise conservative thresholds can erase plausible families without enough information to falsify them.
Universal dataset debt can make future discovery impossible while dataset switching resets debt artificially; family/cohort budgets plus global oversight better match actual selection history.
